# resilience

Timeouts before retries, retry with backoff+jitter, circuit breaker and bulkhead - the AWS Builders' Library canon behind the AF-RES family and AF-PERF-005/007.

## Detected anti-patterns

### `AF-PERF-005` — Timeouts exist before retries, and retries carry jitter (high)

A retry without a timeout waits forever; retries without jitter synchronize into thundering herds. Order matters: connect/read timeouts first, bounded retries with exponential backoff + jitter second, circuit breaker third.

Remediation: Declare connect and total timeouts per dependency; cap attempts; add full jitter; stop retrying on 4xx and on open breakers.

Reference: docs/specs/2026-09-21-api-forge-agentic-platform.md

### `AF-PERF-007` — Sync work does not block the request path unnecessarily (medium)

Calls that outlive their value inside the request (emails, analytics, third-party writes with no response need) stretch p99 for work the caller never sees.

Remediation: Move fire-and-forget work behind a queue/event; keep in-path only calls whose results shape the response; document which downstream calls are on the critical path.

Reference: docs/specs/2026-09-21-api-forge-agentic-platform.md

### `AF-PERF-101` — HTTP call site without a visible timeout (high)

A blocking call with no timeout inherits the TCP defaults — a hung dependency holds the worker until the OS gives up, which is the classic pool-exhaustion cascade. The rule fires only on call sites where no timeout is visible in the surrounding lines.


Remediation: Pass an explicit timeout (connect + read where the client splits them) sized under the caller's SLO.

Reference: https://docs.python-requests.org/en/latest/user/advanced/#timeouts

### `AF-PERF-102` — Retry without backoff (medium)

Retrying immediately turns a struggling dependency into a retry storm; every retry lands on a service that has not recovered.


Remediation: Use exponential backoff with a capped max wait between attempts.

Reference: https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/architecture/exponential-backoff-and-jitter/

### `AF-PERF-103` — Retry without jitter (low)

Even with backoff, synchronized retries herd: every client retries at the same computed instant and re-collides. Jitter decorrelates them.


Remediation: Add full or decorrelated jitter to the backoff schedule.

Reference: https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/architecture/exponential-backoff-and-jitter/

### `AF-PERF-104` — Retry wrapping a mutating call (high)

Retrying a write whose effect already landed produces duplicates unless the operation is idempotent — the pattern match cannot see an idempotency key, so the finding names the retry site to confirm.


Remediation: Retry mutating calls only with an idempotency key, or make the retry idempotent by checking state first.

Reference: https://aws.amazon.com/builders-library/making-retries-safe-with-idempotent-APIs/

### `AF-PERF-105` — No circuit breaker declared in the project (medium)

Without a breaker, every caller keeps paying full latency to a dead dependency. Absence is measured as a project-level scan result — the blind spot is named when the scan saw nothing to scan.


Remediation: Introduce a circuit breaker (resilience4j, pybreaker, gobreaker, Polly) around dependency calls.

Reference: https://martinfowler.com/bliki/CircuitBreaker.html

### `AF-PERF-106` — Connection pool usage without a visible bound (medium)

An unbounded pool exhausts memory or the database under load; the bound is the resilience mechanism, not a tuning detail.


Remediation: Declare max pool size and queueing behavior for every pooled resource.

Reference: https://docs.python.org/3/library/queue.html

### `AF-PERF-107` — No graceful shutdown hook declared in the project (medium)

In-flight requests and buffered writes die with the process; the shutdown hook is what lets drain happen before exit.


Remediation: Register a shutdown hook (@PreDestroy, signal handler, defer Close, atexit) that drains in-flight work.

Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/reliability-pillar/

### `AF-PERF-108` — No idempotency mechanism declared in the project (medium)

Retries and at-least-once delivery mean every mutating operation will eventually arrive twice; without a dedup mechanism the second arrival mutates again.


Remediation: Add idempotency keys or a deduplication mechanism on mutating operations.

Reference: https://aws.amazon.com/builders-library/making-retries-safe-with-idempotent-APIs/
